summary: A round-up of NBL Round 5 results from AAP. Melbourne United extended their winning streak to six and sit atop the ladder, Tyler Harvey's last-second three gave the Illawarra Hawks an 84-83 win over the Cairns Taipans, and the Adelaide 36ers upset the New Zealand Breakers as import Zylan Cheatham went down injured. Other games covered Brisbane's wins over Tasmania and Perth, the Taipans beating Sydney while losing Patrick Miller to a back injury, and South East Melbourne Phoenix narrowly holding off the Breakers.
one_line: NBL Round 5 recap: Harvey's buzzer-beating three sinks Cairns, Melbourne United stay top, and Cheatham is injured as Adelaide upset the Breakers.
key_facts: Chris Goulding scored 33 points with a season-high seven three-pointers as Melbourne United beat the Illawarra Hawks 96-84 at John Cain Arena, extending United's winning streak to six games and their record to 8-1.

Melbourne United played without injured guards Ian Clark (hamstring) and Matthew Dellavedova (concussion) against Illawarra; Luke Travers briefly left with a left knee knock but returned to finish with six points and 11 rebounds.
Tyler Harvey hit a deep three-pointer with one second remaining to give the Illawarra Hawks an 84-83 upset win over the Cairns Taipans at WIN Entertainment Centre, lifting Illawarra to 2-4.
Hawks coach Jacob Jackomas said of Harvey: "That's why we have him"; Patrick Miller had given Cairns a two-point lead with a jump shot in the final 10 seconds and scored 24 points.

Brisbane beat Tasmania 90-87 behind Nathan Sobey's game-high 28 points, without suspended Aron Baynes and injured Shannon Scott, levelling their record at 4-4; it was their first Sunday win after seven straight losses.
Tasmania JackJumpers lost twice in round five, to Melbourne United 90-82 at home and then to Brisbane, falling to 4-4 after a 4-2 start.
Brisbane Bullets beat the Perth Wildcats 84-79 at RAC Arena; Bryce Cotton managed 10 points on 3-of-19 shooting and Perth lost a fourth straight.

Taipans import Patrick Miller, ranked second in NBL scoring, suffered a back injury 1:09 before halftime of Cairns' 87-80 win over Sydney, with Bul Kuol (24 points) and Sam Waardenburg (22) stepping up.
South East Melbourne Phoenix beat the New Zealand Breakers 103-100 after leading by 26; Parker Jackson-Cartwright scored 33 for the Breakers, who suffered a fourth successive defeat.
Dean Vickerman celebrated his 300th NBL game as coach when Melbourne United beat Tasmania 90-82 on Friday night to go 7-1.
Zylan Cheatham (17 points, eight rebounds) hurt his leg early in the fourth quarter as the Adelaide 36ers beat the Breakers 97-85 at Spark Arena; the Sixers won the final quarter 27-14.
Dejan Vasiljevic scored 24 points and sank his 200th three-pointer for the 36ers, who were tipped as possible wooden spooners but have won three of their past four games.
Cheatham was later reported as suffering a broken foot, ruling him out of the Phoenix game.
